calls.message: Build a budget tracker CLI in Python. Define monthly budgets per category, record expenses (amount, category, date, note) into a JSON file, reject unknown categories and invalid amounts, report spending per category against the budget, and alert when a category reaches 80% and 100% of its budget. Single file budget_tracker.py, stdlib only.
calls.result:
The spec is written and passes lint with 0 errors and 1 warning. I'm waiting for your approval before any code is written.

The remaining warning is LINT-HY-007 on hypothesis h4, whose wording the linter reads as describing something that won't be built. I rephrased it once and the warning stayed. It doesn't block anything.

**What the spec covers** (all in `forgemyspec-bundle/budget-tracker/spec.yaml`):

| id | kind | statement |
|---|---|---|
| budget_set | boundary | `set-budget CATEGORY AMOUNT` stores a positive monthly budget. |
| expense_stored | boundary | `add` stores amount, category, date and note in the JSON file. |
| unknown_category | boundary | `add` with an unbudgeted category exits non-zero and leaves the file unchanged. |
| invalid_amount | boundary | `add` rejects non-numeric, zero, negative, nan, infinite and over-2-decimal amounts, and malformed dates. It exits non-zero and leaves the file unchanged. `set-budget` applies the same amount rule. |
| report_spending | boundary | `report --month YYYY-MM` prints spent, budget and percent per category, counting only that month. |
| alert_80 | boundary | A category at 80% or more, but below 100%, prints a warning. Below 80% prints none. |
| alert_100 | boundary | A category at 100% or more prints an over-budget alert. |
| single_file | boundary | `budget_tracker.py` is one file that imports only the standard library. |

This is a spec-only bundle (no Dafny proofs, since it isn't money-critical logic). Its tests will live in `tests/test_budget_tracker.py`.

**Assumptions I made. Tell me if any are wrong:**
- Each category has one monthly limit that applies to every calendar month, with no rollover.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` and months are `YYYY-MM`.
- Amounts use `Decimal` and allow at most 2 decimal places.
- The data file is `budget_data.json` in the current directory, and `--file` overrides it.
- `report` defaults to the current month.
- The only subcommands are `set-budget`, `add` and `report`.

To approve, type this code in the chat: **M6UNKF**. It approves `forgemyspec-bundle/budget-tracker` (content hash e02c8abc41ee). I'll then run `approve` and move on to implementation.

calls.result:
The budget tracker is built, and the gate passes (`RESULT: PASS`, 8 tests, 0 failed).

I did not register this request on the requirements board, so the board still shows 0 requirements.

- **Commands:** `budget_tracker.py` is one stdlib-only file with three subcommands: `set-budget CATEGORY AMOUNT`, `add AMOUNT CATEGORY [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--note ...]` and `report [--month YYYY-MM]`. `--file` picks the JSON file, and `budget_data.json` in the current directory is the default.
- **Rejections:** `add` rejects an unbudgeted category, a non-numeric, zero, negative, nan, infinite or over-2-decimal amount, and a bad date. Each exits non-zero with an error and leaves the file untouched. `set-budget` applies the same amount check.
- **Alerts:** a category at 80% or more of its budget prints a WARNING, and at 100% or more an ALERT. `add` prints it when the expense pushes that month over the line, and `report` shows it for every category.
- **Tests:** the boundary tests are in `tests/test_budget_tracker.py`.

The first gate run failed because my import-check test used `sys.stdlib_module_names`, which this Python version lacks. I replaced it with an explicit list of allowed modules.

The linter warning on hypothesis h4 (LINT-HY-007) is still there. It doesn't block the gate. Clearing it means amending the spec, which needs your approval, so say if you want it.
